answer: Sybils meet burst-capacity attestation. Each identity locks collateral in a vault; weekly, a random committee fires a gale of signed compute probes, and each agent must return verifiable results within 90 seconds, at ninety percent success. Like an echo off a canyon wall, each probe returns only from the key-holding machine, so rented idle servers cannot fake presence: an attacker runs one real CPU hot per identity. Rewards grow sublinearly with identity count, so fifty sybils need fifty always-on machines yet earn under fifty shares, draining the vault faster than yield.
